questions.question: The cost of a washing machine is 40% less than the cost of a TV. If the cost of the washing machine increases by 18% and that of the TV decreases by 10%, then what is the change in the total cost of 5 washing machines and 2 TVs?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost of washing machine is 40% less than cost of tv

Cost of washing machine increases by 18% 

Cost of TV decreases by 10% 

**Formula used:**

Percentage change = (New value - Original value)over Original value × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the cost of TV be 100x 

Then, the cost of washing machine is 40% less = 100x × (60)/(100) = 60x 

Now, the cost of washing machine increases by 18% 

⇒ 60x + 60x × (18)/(100) = 70.8x

Also, the cost of TV decreases by 10%

⇒ 100x × (90)/(100) = 90x 

Initially, the total cost of 5 washing machines and 2 TV = 5 × 60x + 2 × 100x = 500x 

New cost after increasing and decreasing = 5 × 70.8x + 2 × 90x = 534x 

Difference in total costs = (534x - 500x) = 34x 

Percentage increase = ((34x)/(500x)) × 100 = 6.8%

**Hence, there is an increase of 6.8% in the overall cost.**

Simplify the equation directly to find its standard form.

x(x + 3) − 8 = 2(x² − 9)

⇒ x² + 3x − 8 = 2x² − 18

⇒ x² − 3x − 10 = 0

Factorise to get: (x − 5)(x + 2) = 0. The roots are 5 and −2.

Since 5 ≠ −2, the roots are real and distinct.

**∴ The correct answer is Two real and distinct roots.**

For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0,

Discriminant (D) = b² − 4ac

If D > 0, roots are real and distinct.

If D = 0, roots are real and equal.

If D 0, the roots are real and distinct.

**∴ The correct answer is Two real and distinct roots.**

Sum and Product of Roots

• **e= -N (ϕ/dt)**
 
• Where** "e" is the magnitude** of the induced emf, **"N" is the number of turns **on the coil, and** "ϕ" is the amount of magnetic flux** that connects the coil. __
 
• **Focal length**

 
 
• The focal length of a mirror or lens is the distance between its** focal point and its pole**, also known as the **optical center of the lens.**
 
• After reflecting in the mirror, a **parallel beam of light** is "focused" at the focal point (F) of the device.
 
• In the case of a** convex mirror** and lens, the focal length is regarded as **positive.**
 
• It is considered a **negative for a concave mirror **and lens. The letter f denotes it.

• **Convex mirror**

questions.question: An object is placed in front of a convex mirror of focal length 9 cm, at a distance of 18 cm. The magnification produced by the mirror is ________.
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Given,

Focal length, f = +9 {cm} 

Object distance, u = -18 {cm} 

Using the mirror formula:

 (1)/(f) = (1)/(v) + (1)/(u) 

 (1)/(9) = (1)/(v) + (1)/(-18) 

⇒ (1)/(v) = (1)/(9) + (1)/(18) 

⇒ (1)/(v) = (2+1)/(18) = (3)/(18) = (1)/(6) 

⇒ v = 6 {cm} 

Now, using the magnification formula:

 m = (-v)/(u) 

⇒ m = (-6)/(-18) = (1)/(3) 

∴ The magnification produced by the mirror is 1/3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Magnification of mirror

 
 
• Spherical mirrors increase the size of the image relative to the size of the object to produce magnification.
 
• The value of m is the ratio of the image's height to the object's height.
 
• A spherical mirror's magnification, m, can be expressed as:
 
 
• m= h'/h
 
• In this case, h denotes the image's height, and h' denotes the object's height.
 
• The object's height is always positive because it is always above the principal axis. However, the kind of image that is created may alter the height sign. When compared to the height of actual images, the height of virtual images should be considered positive.
 
 
 
• Magnification is also equal to the distance between the object and the image.
 
 
• m= -v/u
 
 
 
• The image is virtual and erect when the magnification is positive.
 
• The image is real and inverted when the magnification is negative.

questions.question: Under perfect competition, a firm earns _________ profits in the long run.

The correct answer is __**Normal**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the long run, **all factors of production are variable**. Also, two of the assumptions of firms in perfect competition are free entry and exit, as well as perfect resource mobility.
 
• In the long run, firms making an abnormal profit will attract new firms, which will enter freely due to the **two assumptions already stated**.

questions.question: Three pipes A, B and C together can fill a tank in 8 hours. Three pipes were opened for 2 hours, after that C was closed. Later A and B fill the remaining part in 9 hours. The number of hours taken by C alone to fill the tank is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A, B, and C together fill the tank completely in 8 hours

A, B, and C worked for 2 hours and then the remaining work is done by A and B in 9 hours.

**Concept used:**

Efficiency × Time = Work

**Calculation:**

Let the efficiency of pipes be A, B, and C respectively.

Total work = LCM(8 hours) = 8 

Efficiency of A + B + C = (8)/(8) = 1

Now, According to the question,

Total work done by A, B, and C together in 8 hours = work done by A, B, and C in 2 hours + Work done by A and B in 9 hours

(A + B + C) × 8 = (A + B + C) × 2 + (A + B) × 9

⇒ 8( A + B + C) - 2(A + B + C) = 9(A + B)

⇒ 6(A + B + C) = 9(A + B)

⇒ 6C = 3(A + B)

⇒ 2C = A + B

Now, We have

(A + B + C) × 8 = C × Time

⇒ (2C + C) × 8 = C × Time

⇒ 24C = C × Time

⇒ Time = 24 hours

**Hence, The number of hours taken by C alone to fill the tank is 24 hours.**

questions.question: The HCF of the numbers 310, 208 and 180 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the smallest difference between any two given numbers: 208 − 180 = 28.

The HCF must be a factor of this difference. The factors of 28 are 28, 14, 7, 4, 2, and 1.

The number 310 is not perfectly divisible by 28, 14, 7, or 4.

Since 310, 208, and 180 are all even numbers, they are all perfectly divisible by 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 310, 208, and 180.

**Method Used:**

Prime Factorization Method: The HCF is the product of the lowest power of all common prime factors.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 310 = 2 × 5 × 31

⇒ 208 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 13 = 2⁴ × 13

⇒ 180 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 2² × 3² × 5

⇒ The only common prime factor among all three numbers is 2.

⇒ The lowest power of 2 present in the factorizations is 2¹ = 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The HCF of two or more numbers is the largest positive integer that divides each of the numbers without leaving a remainder.

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The LCM of two or more numbers is the smallest positive integer that is perfectly divisible by each of the given numbers.

Product of Two Numbers Rule

For any two numbers a and b: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b). Note that this property applies only to two numbers, not three.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are considered co-prime (or mutually prime) if their Highest Common Factor (HCF) is exactly 1.

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics of the pea plant was NOT used by Mendel in his experiments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Shape of leaves__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mendel experiments**

 
 
• ​Mendel conducted experiments on a **pea plant** and identified seven primary traits that distinguished the plants. He then carried out the two experiments to ascertain the** inheritance rules**.
 
 
 
• **The two experiments are described in detail below.**
 
• **Monohybrid Cross**
 
 
• Mendel crossed two oppositely shaped pea plants—**one short and one tall**—in this experiment.
 
• He named the offspring from the first generation **F1 progeny** because they were tall.
 
• After that, he crossed F1 offspring, which resulted in tall and short plants in a** 3:1 ratio.**
 
 
 
• **Dihybrid Cross**
 
 
• Mendel looked at **two traits** with two alleles in a dihybrid cross-experiment.
 
• He noticed that all of the offspring of the first generation, or **F1 offspring**, were **round-yellow** after crossing **wrinkled-green** seeds with** round-yellow seeds.**
 
• This indicated that the **round shape** and **yellow color **were the dominant characteristics.
 
• After that, he **self-pollinated** the F1 offspring, resulting in four distinct traits: in the ratio of **9:3:3:1**, the seeds are **round-yellow, round-green, wrinkled-yellow, and wrinkled-green.**
 
 

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mendel’s laws**

 
 
• **Law of Dominance:** Mendel's **first law of inheritance** is also used to refer to this.
 
• **Hybrid offspring** will only inherit the dominant phenotype trait, according to the law of dominance.
 
• **Recessive traits **are those in which alleles are suppressed, while dominant traits are those in which alleles are present.
 
• **Law of Segregation:** According to the law of segregation, two copies of each hereditary factor segregate during the production of gametes, giving offspring one factor from each parent.
 
• To put it another way, **allele pairs**—the gene's alternative form—segregate during the gamete's formation and randomly reunite during fertilization. Mendel's **third law of inheritance** is another name for this one.
 
• **Law of Independent Assortment:** The law of independent assortment, also known as **Mendel's second law of inheritance**, states that a pair of traits segregates independently of another pair during **gamete formation**.
 
• Different characteristics have equal chances of occurring together because the individual **heredity factors **assort independently.

questions.question: The hydrocarbons which have a double bond between two carbon atoms are called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__unsaturated compounds__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Unsaturated compounds**

 
 
• **​Organic compounds** known as unsaturated hydrocarbons are characterized by the presence of a **double or triple bond** between two carbon atoms that are adjacent to one another and are entirely composed of hydrogen and carbon.
 
• The position of the double or triple bond is either described by a number written before the compound's name in the **IUPAC nomenclature **of unsaturated **hydrocarbons** (as in 2,4 pentadiene) or by a number written before the suffix, such as** "-ene" or "-yne,"** (as in pent-2-ene).
 
• **Alkenes** and olefins are hydrocarbons that have **at least one double bond** between two adjacent carbon atoms.
 
• **Alkynes** are hydrocarbons that have** at least one triple bond **between two carbon atoms that are right next to each other.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saturated compounds**

 
 
• **​**A saturated hydrocarbon is one in which every **single carbon-carbon bond** is present.
 
• **Carbon and hydrogen** are the only components of an organic compound known as a **hydrocarbon.**
 
• **Saturated hydrocarbons**, as the name suggests, are hydrocarbons in which all of the carbon atoms are bonded to four other atoms and are "saturated," indicating that these organic compounds lack multiple** carbon-carbon bonds.**
 
• The** carbon chains of alkanes** can be either straight or branched.
 
• These saturated hydrocarbons have **sp3 hybridization** on every carbon atom.
 
• **Cycloalkanes** have sp3 hybridized carbon atoms arranged in a **ring**. Saturated hydrocarbons, on the other hand, have a ring that can form side chains.

__
 
• **Newlands' Law of Octaves**

 
 
• **​British chemist John Newlands** attempted the **62 elements **that were known at the time in **1864.**
 
• Based on their **atomic masses**, he arranged them in ascending order and discovered that each **eighth element **shared similar properties.** Newland's law of octaves** was developed based on this observation.
 
• The law of octaves states that every eighth element has similar properties when the elements are arranged in the **increasing order **of their atomic masses.
 
• The** octaves** of music, in which every eighth note is comparable to the first, was used by Newlands to illustrate the similarity between the elements.

• **Limitations of Newland’s Law of Octaves**

 
 
• **​**In **Newland's periodic classification**, a number of elements shared the** same slots**.
 
• **Nickel and cobalt**, for instance, were inserted into the same slot.
 
• Some metals, like cobalt, nickel, and platinum, were included in the group that included the **halogens.**
 
• Only elements up to **calcium** were subject to Newland's law of octaves.
 
• Octaves were unable to accommodate elements with **higher atomic masses.**
 
• The **octave pattern** could not accommodate the subsequent discoveries of **elements**.

questions.question: ________ is spoken by around 2.5 million people, mainly on the central west coast of India, and it is the official language of Goa.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Konkani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Konkani language, **Indo-Aryan language** of the **Indo-European language family**. Konkani is spoken by some **2.5 million** people, mainly on the central west coast of India, where it is the **official language of Goa state**. 
 
• It is also associated particularly with **the city of Mangalore** (Mangaluru) in southwestern Karnataka and is spoken especially along the **west coast of Maharashtra state**.
 
• It is one of the **22 Scheduled languages** mentioned in the 8th schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Konkani people kept the language alive as a dialect in their homes and social gatherings in this area. Konkani is an **Indo-Aryan language** derived from the mother of all **Indian languages, Sanskrit and Prakrit language**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **substratum** of the Konkani language lies in the speech of **Austroasiatic tribes** called **Kurukh**, Oraon, and Kukni, whose modern representatives are languages like Kurukh and its dialects including **Kurux, Kunrukh, Kunna, and Malto**.
 
• According to the **Indian Anthropological Society**, these Australoid tribes speaking **Austro-Asiatic** or **Munda languages** who once inhabited Konkan migrated to Northern India (Chota Nagpur Plateau, Mirzapur) and are not found in Konkan anymore.
 
• The grammatical impact of the **Dravidian languages** on the structure and syntax of **Indo-Aryan languages** is difficult to fathom. Some linguists explain this anomaly by arguing that Middle Indo-Aryan and New Indo-Aryan were built on a Dravidian **substratum.**
 
• Some examples of Konkani words of Dravidian origin are: **naall** (coconut), **madval** (washerman), **choru** (cooked rice), and **mulo** (radish).
